title: React Module 02 Core Check
description: Check your understanding of components, JSX, props, state, children, composition, and prop patterns.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: Read-only inputs passed from a parent component
Local variables that always trigger renders
Database records owned by a component

questions.explanation: Props are inputs passed down from parent to child and should be treated as read-only.

options.text: Data a component needs to remember between renders
Only values passed from children to parents

questions.explanation: State is component-owned data that React remembers and uses when rendering.

questions.prompt: Which values can commonly be passed as props? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Props can be any JavaScript value, including functions used as callbacks.

questions.prompt: How is the special `children` prop usually supplied?

options.text: By placing content between a component opening and closing tag

questions.explanation: React passes nested JSX content as the `children` prop.

questions.prompt: A child component should directly mutate a prop object to notify its parent about a change.
questions.explanation: Props are read-only. Children should communicate changes through callbacks or parent-managed state.

questions.prompt: What does lifting state up mean?

options.text: Moving shared state to the nearest common parent

questions.explanation: State is lifted when multiple components need to read or update the same data.

questions.prompt: Which JSX passes a string prop named `label`?

options.text: `<Button label={Save} />` when Save is not defined

questions.explanation: String props can be passed with quoted attributes in JSX.

questions.prompt: Which are common component design practices? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Use props to configure reusable pieces
Store all app data in every child component

questions.explanation: Focused, configurable, composed components are easier to reuse and reason about.
